subject: Civil Engineering
title: Foundation Requirements
description: A short lesson to help you apply Foundation Requirements.

hook.text: A dam is only as strong as what it stands on — the foundation determines everything.

buildup.text: Rock foundations are ideal — they resist compression and provide anchorage for arch dams.

discovery.text: Soil foundations work for embankment dams — but settlement must be controlled carefully.

twist.text: Grout curtains — injected cement walls underground — block seepage paths through fractured rock.

climax.text: Foundation preparation can cost 30% of the total dam budget — it's that critical.

punchline.text: Build a perfect dam on a weak foundation and it fails. The ground comes first.

quiz.question: What is a grout curtain in dam construction?
options: A decorative concrete wall on the downstream face
Injected cement that forms an underground wall to block seepage through fractured rock
A sheet of waterproof fabric draped over the dam face

details.summary: Dam foundations must support the structure's weight, resist water pressure forces, and prevent excessive seepage beneath the dam. Foundation investigation includes drilling, rock testing, permeability measurement, and geological mapping.
details.whyItMatters: Foundation inadequacy is a leading cause of dam failure. The foundation is often the weakest link in the dam system, making thorough investigation and treatment essential for safe performance.
takeaways: Rock foundations are preferred for concrete dams while soil suits embankment dams
Grout curtains inject cement into rock fractures to reduce seepage paths
Drainage galleries collect seepage and reduce dangerous uplift pressure

faq.question: What is a grout curtain beneath a dam?
faq.answer: A grout curtain is a barrier created by drilling holes into rock beneath the dam and injecting cement grout under pressure to fill fractures and voids. This reduces permeability and creates a relatively watertight zone that limits seepage beneath the dam.

faq.question: Why is geological investigation so critical before dam construction?
faq.answer: Unexpected geological conditions like faults, solution cavities, weak clay seams, or high permeability zones have caused numerous dam failures. Investigation through drilling, testing.
